classification.difficultyReason: Use similar-triangle ratios for the supports and Pythagoras for the slope, then identify every timber member in two frames and interpret whole-metre purchasing before costing. Earlier parts supply the lengths needed for the final calculation.

content.prompt: A builder is constructing a ramp $AB$, as drawn in the diagram, with $BC=2$ metres and $AC=6$ metres. Two vertical supports $ED$ and $GF$ need to be placed at 2-metre intervals.

spec.description: A horizontal base A-D-F-C supports the sloping ramp AB. Vertical members DE, FG and CB meet the base at right angles. Ordinary source blue members are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AD=DF=FC=2 m; BC=2 m; A,E,G,B are collinear; DE,FG,BC are perpendicular to AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions, vertex labels, frame members and right-angle markers are visible.

answer.worked:
Triangles $ADE$ and $ACB$ are similar (AAA): both have a right angle and share the angle at $A$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DE}{BC}&=\frac{AD}{AC}\\\frac{DE}{2}&=\frac{2}{6}\\DE&=\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

Triangles $AFG$ and $ACB$ are similar (AAA): both have a right angle and share the angle at $A$. Also, $AF=2+2=4$ m.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{FG}{BC}&=\frac{AF}{AC}\\\frac{FG}{2}&=\frac{4}{6}\\FG&=\frac{4}{3}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

By Pythagoras’ theorem in right-angled triangle $ACB$:
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=AC^2+BC^2\\AB^2&=6^2+2^2\\AB^2&=40\\AB&=2\sqrt{10}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The builder needs to construct two timber frames (as drawn in the diagram) to support the ramp.

children.label: i
children.prompt: What length of timber, to the nearest metre, will he need?

answer.worked:
Each frame contains $AC$, $CB$, $BA$, $DE$ and $FG$. For two frames, the total length $L$ is:
$$\begin{align*}L&=2\left(6+2+2\sqrt{10}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{4}{3}\right)\\L&=20+4\sqrt{10}\text{ m}\\L&\approx32.6491\text{ m}\\L&\approx33\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre)}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Timber costs $\$4.60$ per metre and is only sold in lengths which are a multiple of one metre. How much will the timber cost the builder?

answer.worked:
The total required is $20+4\sqrt{10}\approx32.6491$ m, so at least $33$ whole metres must be bought. Offcuts can be used for the shorter supports.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost}&=33\times\$4.60\\\text{Cost}&=\$151.80.\end{align*}$$
